pages.note: New section on validating messages between a content script and the background. Every MessageSender field (id, url, origin, tab, frameId) and its description read from developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/api/runtime and developer.mozilla.org runtime/MessageSender. Per-browser availability read from mdn/browser-compat-data webextensions/api/runtime.json: origin is Chrome 80 and Firefox 126, tlsChannelId and documentLifecycle have no Firefox support. externally_connectable semantics (absent key: all extensions, no web pages; ids with the * wildcard; matches for web pages; external senders land on onMessageExternal and onConnectExternal) read from the Chrome manifest reference and the Chrome messaging guide, which also supplies the content-scripts-are-less-trustworthy and no-eval guidance. Firefox has no externally_connectable (BCD, bugzil.la/1319168) and Safari 15.4 supports only matches (BCD notes). port.sender presence on onConnect and onConnectExternal ports read from the Chrome runtime reference. The dev-time bridge detail (a port named __extjs-bridge-log__ to the service worker, the devtools page relaying through runtime.sendMessage with an __extjsBridgeLog key, nothing of it in production) read from programs/develop/dev-server/control-bridge/producer-runtime.ts and plugin-reload/steps/inject-bridge-relay.ts, and confirmed by grepping a production build made with the published extension@4.1.31 (content template): zero matches for either marker in dist/chromium. A second change in the same batch added the first-screen sentence (Extension.js builds and runs browser extensions from one manifest.json for Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari, plus the npx extension@latest start command), checked the same way as the other first-screen pages in this batch.

New section on telling content script rows from service worker rows. Flags and the context list verified with `npx -y extension@4.1.31 logs --help`. Context assignment per compiled entry (content_scripts/ is content, action/index.js is popup, options/index.js is options, the background producer defaults to background) read from programs/develop/plugin-reload/steps/inject-bridge-relay.ts RELAY_TARGETS and dev-server/control-bridge/producer-runtime.ts. Content rows carrying url, tabId and frameId from the relaying sender, and background rows carrying none of them, read from shipRelayedLog and the background console hook in producer-runtime.ts. No producer sets a hostname field, so the section does not name one. The --url matcher returning false when a row has no url or hostname, --tab comparing tabId, --context refusing unknown names, console.log printing as LOG and filtering as info, and uncaught errors and unhandled rejections shipping as level error with the stack appended, all read from programs/extension/commands/logs.ts (makeUrlMatcher, makeFilter, levelToken, formatPrettyLogLine) and producer-runtime.ts (shipUncaughtError). The jq expression was run against two synthetic ndjson rows and produced the expected two tab-separated lines. The sample LOG lines reuse the console.log strings of the content template scaffolded by the published CLI. dev --logs and --log-context read from programs/extension/commands/dev.ts and are already documented on the dev page. A second change in the same batch added the first-screen sentence (Extension.js builds and runs browser extensions from one manifest.json for Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari, plus the npx extension@latest start command), checked the same way as the other first-screen pages in this batch.

New section on trimming what ships. Verified on a project created with `npx -y extension@4.1.31 create trim-demo --template content --install`. Unreferenced files added to src/ (notes.md, unused.js, images/unused-photo.png, content/fixtures/sample.json, content/README.md) were absent from dist/chromium after `npx extension build`. public/banner.png and public/fonts/Inter.woff2 landed at dist/chromium/banner.png and dist/chromium/fonts/Inter.woff2. The template's images/icon.png, imported from the content script and referenced from the options HTML, shipped three times (assets/icon.520a6fe7.png, assets/images/icon.png, images/icon.png, 35.77 KB each), which matches the source-path copy in plugin-web-extension/feature-html/steps/add-assets-to-compilation.ts and the hashed JS asset. The HTML plugin skipping emission for public-root references read from the same file. web_accessible_resources in the built manifest held 790.js (the import() chunk), assets/icon.520a6fe7.png and assets/images/icon.png under <all_urls>, and no public/ file, matching the fallback in feature-web-resources/web-resources-lib/generate-manifest.ts that exposes every non-script assets/ file and every content script async chunk under the union of content script matches. The size line `Extension built for production in dist/chromium (171.6 KB)`, the `Packaged dist/trimdemo-1.0.0-chromium.zip (142.9 KB)` line, the archive holding only the dist/chromium files (unzip -l, 17 entries), the json envelope fields total_bytes, largest_asset_bytes and zip_artifacts[].size, and dist/extension-js/chromium/build-summary.json carrying the same fields, all read from the actual build output. The zip name derivation (manifest name lowercased, non-alphanumerics dropped, -<version>-<browser>) read from plugin-compilation/zip.ts sanitize().
